title: Time Jump: 06:30, Heavy Rain Arrives Early

fields.narration: EXERCISE EXERCISE EXERCISE. It is now 06:30 EDT, Thursday, March 25, 2027. It is still dark. Sunrise is about 07:20. Since 06:10 the rain has turned heavy. The radar band that NWS expected between 07:00 and 10:00 is arriving early over the hills north of campus. The Mill Street gauge reads 5.55 ft and is rising about 1.6 ft per hour, faster than the 1.5 ft per hour in the Annex F flood profile. At the culvert mouth, Tech 4 reports that limbs are racking on the trash rack faster than one person can clear them. The Riverside basement laundry opened at 06:30 as scheduled. The tanker supplier's dispatcher is still waiting for an answer, and the 06:45 deadline is 15 minutes away. Whatever activation level and orders the IC set in Phase 1 stay in force. Anything not decided is still undecided.
worldState: Clock: 06:30 EDT, Thursday, March 25, 2027. Dark until sunrise at about 07:20.
Weather: heavy rain over the Sugar Camp Run basin. The heaviest rain is arriving ahead of the 7 AM to 10 AM window in the 517 AM Flash Flood Watch. The watch is still in effect for Athens County.
MSU stage gauge, Mill Street culvert: 5.55 ft at 06:30, trend RISING at about +1.6 ft/hr. Action stage is 5.0 ft and flood stage is 7.0 ft.
Mill Street culvert: debris is racking on the trash rack faster than Tech 4 can clear it alone. Tech 4 is still on the bridge.
Dairy Lane crossing: still open. The crossing closes at 6.5 ft.
Diesel tanker: due at 08:00 by the Dairy Lane crossing. The supplier's dispatcher needs an answer by 06:45: call off, pull in early or re-route. The Kessler generator day tank is at about half.
Lot C: 9 Facilities trucks and both mobile generators on trailers are still parked there unless Facilities ordered them moved in Phase 1. A full move takes a crew about 40 minutes.
Riverside basement: the laundry room opened at 06:30. The custodial crew is still scheduled into the mechanical room at 07:00 for a filter change.
Riverside: 680 residents, most still asleep. RAs are waiting to hear whether to wake their floors. Sugar Run Apartments: 210 residents.
08:00 classes are still on the schedule. Many Riverside residents walk to class across the Lower Quad.
Every activation level, order and public message from Phase 1 stays in force. Anything not decided is still undecided.
fields.facilitatorNote: At +1.6 ft/hr the gauge reaches the 6.5 ft Dairy Lane closure at about 07:05 and flood stage (7.0 ft) at about 07:25. Do not say this; let the seats work it out. If no seat has answered the tanker dispatcher by 06:45, the SimCell calls Facilities to say the driver is leaving on the usual Dairy Lane route.
fields.scenarioTitle: Ninety Minutes: Flash Flood, Evacuation & Campus Shelter

instructorNote: This card starts Phase 2. Every seat should update the projector situation summary, and the IC should confirm the activation level and log its time and basis under EOP Annex F section 4. Facilities must answer the tanker supplier before 06:45, and the Dean of Students and Facilities must decide on the Riverside basement before the 07:00 mechanical-room crew goes in.
